pr.title: GVN: stop hashing opaque values
pr.description:
GVN generates values that are not meant to be unified with any other. For instance `Opaque` (aka we don't know anything), non-deterministic constants and borrows.

The current algorithm generates a unique index, so the generated `Value` will be different from all the existing. This is wasteful, as we should not hash that `Value` at all.

This PR proposes to do this. This involves partially reimplementing a `FxIndexSet`, but yields a small but consistent perf improvement (https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/pull/145737#issuecomment-3276951054).

analysis.incorrectTransformation: Treating every `Value` variant uniformly as hashable/deduplicable, including values whose distinctness comes from an external uniqueness counter. The concrete pre-PR behavior is an `FxIndexSet<(Value, Ty)>` insertion of `Opaque`, `Address` provenance, and non-deterministic `Constant` disambiguators. This is not a behavior-changing miscompile in the historical code because the unique counter prevented equality; the correctness hazard is that any rewrite that deduplicates these variants (or reuses/forgets the uniqueness disambiguator) can merge distinct opaque states, distinct borrow/pointer provenances, or separate mentions of a non-deterministic constant. The new invariant is the inverse transformation: unique-by-construction values bypass hashing/deduplication entirely (`insert_unique`, always a new index), while only genuinely deduplicable values go through `insert`.
analysis.inputDomain: MIR bodies processed by GVN that contain (a) opaque values created for unknown state, (b) borrows/pointers whose provenance must stay distinct, (c) non-deterministic constants where each mention must remain a different value, and (d) deref invalidation that turns an existing value opaque. Deterministic constants, scalars, and booleans remain in the deduplicable domain.
analysis.originalLogic: GVN stored every `(Value, Ty)` pair in an `FxIndexSet`, using `insert_full` for all insertions. Root values that must remain distinct already carried a fresh counter: `Value::Opaque(usize)`, `Value::Address { provenance: usize, .. }`, and `Value::Constant { disambiguator: usize, .. }` where a nonzero disambiguator marked a non-deterministic constant. Because the counter was unique, the set hashed and compared these values but could never find an equal existing entry. `invalidate_derefs` also created a new counter and overwrote the stored value with a fresh `Value::Opaque`.
pitfalls: Do not route `Opaque`, `Address`, or non-deterministic `Constant` through the deduplicating `insert` path: their marker type makes hashing/comparison ICE by design.
Do not merge two mentions of the same non-deterministic constant; the source comment requires assigning a different disambiguator so they do not get the same `VnIndex`.
Do not merge borrows or pointers: the source requires giving each a different provenance.
`insert_unique` stores a placeholder hash of 0 and does not add the index to the hash table; unique values therefore cannot be found by later deduplication, which is intentional.
`forget` mutates a value to opaque without removing its old hash-table entry; equality must guard against treating the forgotten index as the old value.

Do not conclude that the pre-PR code was miscompiling: the PR describes wasted hashing, while the unique counter preserved distinctness. The reusable correctness concern is the invariant that unique values must not be deduplicated.
preconditions: `ValueSet::insert_unique` is restricted by a debug assertion to `Value::Opaque`, `Value::Address`, or `Value::Constant { disambiguator: Some(_), .. }`.
`ValueSet::insert` is restricted by a debug assertion to non-opaque, non-address values and to constants with `disambiguator: None` (deterministic).
`VnOpaque` must only be constructed by `insert_unique`; its `Hash` and `PartialEq` implementations are `unreachable!()` so hashing/comparing it is a compiler ICE.
A non-deterministic constant's `disambiguator` is `Some(VnOpaque)` and must differ per mention; a deterministic constant uses `disambiguator: None`.
Borrow/pointer provenance is a `VnOpaque`; separate borrows/pointers must not share an index.
`forget` replaces a stored value with `Value::Opaque(VnOpaque)` in place rather than inserting a new value, so that index must no longer deduplicate to its old value.
analysis.summary: GVN symbolizes values: most `(Value, Ty)` pairs are deduplicated, but `Opaque`, `Address` borrows/pointers, and non-deterministic constants are unique by construction and must never be unified with another value. The historical implementation hashed and equality-checked every such value in an `FxIndexSet` even though a fresh counter guaranteed uniqueness, wasting work. This PR adds a `ValueSet` with `insert_unique` (no hashing, always a fresh `VnIndex`) and a `VnOpaque` marker whose `Hash`/`PartialEq` are `unreachable!()`, so accidentally hashing or comparing a unique value ICEs instead of silently deduplicating it.
analysis.testStrategy: Unit-test `ValueSet` semantics directly in `compiler/rustc_mir_transform/src/gvn.rs`: (1) two `insert_unique` calls for the same type/opaque produce different `VnIndex` values and neither is retrievable by a later `insert`; (2) two separate non-deterministic constant insertions produce different indices; (3) inserting the same deterministic `(Const, Ty)` twice produces the same index with `new == false`; (4) two address values with different provenance produce different indices; (5) `forget(index)` causes that index's value to be `Opaque` and prevents deduplication against the old value. At MIR level, construct a body with two mentions of a non-deterministic constant and with two distinct borrows/pointers, run GVN, and assert they are not propagated as the same value; also include a deterministic constant that should still be deduplicated. The supplied patch adds no regression test changes (the decoded test diff is `[]`), so these tests are proposed, not historically executed; no compiler run is claimed here.
analysis.trigger: GVN's symbolic execution creates a root value that is intended to be unique: `new_opaque`, address/borrow creation with provenance, insertion of a non-deterministic constant, or invalidation of cached derefs. A deduplicating value set must not hash/merge these; conversely, the ordinary `insert` path must be used for values like deterministic constants that should be unified.
